# What Duffel access tokens the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# Every token here is built from the ordered run 0123456789abcdef, which no real
# credential is. That run is sixteen characters and a body is forty-three, so a
# body carries on through the alphabet to z and then back to 0. Where a case is
# about one position of the body rather than about the count, that position is
# rewritten and the rest of the run is left standing, so the body still comes to
# forty-three.

patterns: duffel-access-token

# The two prefixes Duffel issues an access token with, one to a mode. There is
# no third kind of string here: a token is created read-only or read-write and
# Duffel writes the permission nowhere in it, so nothing in the value says what
# it reaches, and the cases below are the one shape in the places a token is
# written.

case:     a live token in an environment assignment
in:       DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=«duffel-access-token»

case:     a test token in an environment assignment
in:       DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=duffel_test_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=«duffel-access-token»

case:     a token in the bearer authorization header the duffel api is called with
in:       Authorization: Bearer duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      Authorization: Bearer «duffel-access-token»

case:     a token in json
in:       {"access_token":"duffel_test_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456"}
out:      {"access_token":"«duffel-access-token»"}

case:     a token on a command line
in:       curl -H "Authorization: Bearer duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456" https://api.duffel.com/air/orders
out:      curl -H "Authorization: Bearer «duffel-access-token»" https://api.duffel.com/air/orders

case:     a token in a configuration environment block
in:       "env": {"DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "duffel_test_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456"}
out:      "env": {"DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN": "«duffel-access-token»"}

case:     a token in yaml
in:       duffel_access_token: duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_access_token: «duffel-access-token»

case:     a token in a diff line
in:       +DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      +DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN=«duffel-access-token»

case:     a token in a markdown code span
in:       `duffel_test_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456`
out:      `«duffel-access-token»`

# The alphabet the forty-three characters are written in. It is base64url — the
# letters of both cases, the digits, the hyphen and the underscore. The two
# characters standard base64 writes in place of the last of those, the plus sign
# and the slash, are not admitted, and neither is the equals sign a padded
# encoding closes on.

case:     a body written in capitals
in:       duffel_live_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body opening on a hyphen
in:       duffel_live_-123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body closing on a hyphen
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345-
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body opening on an underscore
in:       duffel_live__123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body closing on an underscore
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345_
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body opening on the last letter of the alphabet
in:       duffel_live_z123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body closing on the last letter of the alphabet
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345z
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body carrying a plus sign
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop+rstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop+rstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a body carrying a slash
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop/rstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop/rstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a body carrying an equals sign
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop=rstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop=rstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a dot straight behind the prefix
in:       duffel_live_.123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live_.123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a space straight behind the prefix
in:       duffel_live_ 123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live_ 123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

# The lengths either side of forty-three. The count is read exactly rather than
# as a floor: forty-three base64url characters are the width thirty-two bytes
# encode to, and no other whole number of bytes comes to it. So forty-two
# characters are not a token, and forty-four are a token and the character
# written after it.

case:     a body of forty-three characters is a token
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     a body of forty-two characters is not
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345
out:      duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345

case:     an alphabet run longer than the count is a token and what follows it
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz01234567
out:      «duffel-access-token»7

# The modes. The scan reads the two Duffel names rather than any word standing
# where a mode stands, and the strings below are what that decides: Duffel
# writes its own name in front of a word in its stays response, in its identity
# response and in the user agent its own client libraries send. The second case
# is what a scan reading any word there would locate whole.

case:     a mode no duffel page writes
in:       duffel_prod_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_prod_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a stays rate source with a body behind it
in:       duffel_hotel_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_hotel_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     the rate source as the stays response writes it
in:       {"source":"duffel_hotel_group_rewards"}
out:      {"source":"duffel_hotel_group_rewards"}

case:     the user agent duffel's own client library sends
in:       User-Agent: Duffel/v2 duffel_api_javascript/4.9.0
out:      User-Agent: Duffel/v2 duffel_api_javascript/4.9.0

case:     a field of the identity response
in:       {"is_duffel_links_enabled":true}
out:      {"is_duffel_links_enabled":true}

case:     the prefix written in capitals
in:       DUFFEL_LIVE_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      DUFFEL_LIVE_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     hyphens where the prefix carries underscores
in:       duffel-live-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel-live-0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

# What a token may be written against. There is no boundary on either side of
# the prefix, so a token keeps its span whatever word character it abuts — and
# the count ends it at its fifty-fifth character, so whatever is written after
# one stays in the text whether the alphabet admits it or not.

case:     a token after an underscore
in:       DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN_duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      DUFFEL_ACCESS_TOKEN_«duffel-access-token»

case:     a token after a letter
in:       xduffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      x«duffel-access-token»

case:     a word written against a token
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456suffix
out:      «duffel-access-token»suffix

case:     a hyphenated word written against a token
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456-suffix
out:      «duffel-access-token»-suffix

case:     an underscored word written against a token
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456_suffix
out:      «duffel-access-token»_suffix

case:     a token at the end of a sentence
in:       the token is duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456.
out:      the token is «duffel-access-token».

case:     a token immediately against japanese on both sides
in:       トークンはduffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456です
out:      トークンは«duffel-access-token»です

case:     a token against an invalid byte
in:       \xffduffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456\xff
out:      \xff«duffel-access-token»\xff

# Two tokens written together. Every character of a prefix belongs to the
# alphabet a body is written in, so a prefix can stand inside the body of the
# token before it; the second token begins twelve characters into the first, the
# two spans overlap and are redacted as one. Written with nothing at all between
# them the two are separate values, since the count ends the first where the
# second opens.

case:     a token beginning inside the token before it
in:       duffel_test_duffel_test_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»

case:     two tokens with nothing between them
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456duffel_test_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token»«duffel-access-token»

case:     two tokens separated by a space
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456 duffel_test_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456
out:      «duffel-access-token» «duffel-access-token»

# What this pattern redacts that nobody issued. A prefix holds two underscores,
# which hexadecimal, base62, standard base64 and base32 write nowhere, so only a
# base64url encoding can spell one — and where forty-three characters of the
# alphabet follow, those fifty-five characters are redacted whether or not
# Duffel issued them. Such a run is a token's format exactly and nothing in the
# text tells the two apart, so sparing it would spare a real token written the
# same way.
#
# The digest is the same over-match taking a value a reader had a use for. The
# hexadecimal digits are base64url and a digest carries nothing that ends a run,
# so a SHA-256 written behind a prefix is longer than a body and the first
# forty-three characters of it go with the prefix while the rest stays. What
# holds either side of it is the count and the prefix — a SHA-1 at forty and a
# UUID at thirty-six are short of a body, and a UUID's hyphens are in the
# alphabet, so it is the count that turns one away and not the separators.
#
# The last case is the encoding that carries none of this. Standard base64
# writes + and / where base64url writes the hyphen and the underscore, so a
# certificate body holds no prefix to be found at however long it runs.

case:     the prefix inside a longer run of base64url
in:       payload=zzzzduffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456zzzz
out:      payload=zzzz«duffel-access-token»zzzz

case:     the prefix where a signature stands
in:       eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzzduffel_live_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456zzzz
out:      eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJzdWIiOiJhYmMifQ.zzzz«duffel-access-token»zzzz

case:     a sha256 behind the prefix
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «duffel-access-token»bcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a sha1 behind the prefix, three characters short of a body
in:       duffel_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      duffel_live_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     a uuid behind the prefix
in:       duffel_live_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef
out:      duffel_live_01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef

case:     a sha256 behind a hyphen rather than the prefix
in:       duffel-live-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      duffel-live-0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

case:     a certificate body in standard base64
in:       MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA0123456789abcdef+/0123456789abcdef
out:      MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8AMIIBCgKCAQEA0123456789abcdef+/0123456789abcdef

# The prefix with each of its two underscores dropped in turn, and a body of the
# right length with no prefix at all.

case:     the opening without its underscore
in:       duffellive_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffellive_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     the mode without the underscore that closes it
in:       duffel_live0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      duffel_live0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456

case:     a run of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456
